learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears.

items.title: Starting check: identify the reducing division
items.prompt: A diploid cell produces cells with one homolog from each chromosome pair. Which outcome distinguishes this step from ordinary mitosis?

items.title: Guided practice: trace allele segregation
items.prompt: One homolog carries allele A and its partner carries allele a. After normal meiotic homolog separation, what must be true of a gamete?
options: It receives both A and a homologs
It receives either A or a

items.title: Less help: connect meiosis and fertilization
items.prompt: Why does meiosis help maintain a stable chromosome number across sexual generations?

items.title: Solo practice: compare with mitosis
items.prompt: Which product pattern is expected from one diploid precursor after normal meiosis rather than mitosis?

items.title: Near exit: predict segregation
items.prompt: A cell is heterozygous Dd at one locus on a homolog pair. Ignoring mutation and crossover at that locus, which gamete set is expected?
options: Every gamete carries D and d

items.title: Changed exit: combine independent orientations
items.prompt: Genes A/a and B/b lie on different chromosome pairs. The A-bearing homolog is fixed toward one pole, while the B pair can orient either way. Which two gametes can arise at that pole?

items.title: Repair: inventory one homolog per pair
items.prompt: A normal gamete receives which chromosome inventory from a diploid cell with three homolog pairs?

items.title: Fresh re-entry: trace a new pair
items.prompt: A new homolog pair carries M on one homolog and m on the other. What does normal segregation predict?
options: Each gamete receives M or m

items.title: Repair: keep chromosome pairs separate
items.prompt: If allele R is on chromosome pair 1 and allele T is on pair 2, why can R combine with T or t?
options: R changes into both T and t

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry
items.prompt: A new cell is GgHh with loci on different chromosome pairs. Which set reflects independent assortment before crossover?

items.title: Starting check: identify a tetrad
items.prompt: Two replicated homologous chromosomes align during synapsis. How many chromatids are present in the aligned unit?

items.title: Guided practice: locate recombination
items.prompt: One homolog carries AB and the other carries ab. A crossover occurs between A and B on two non-sister chromatids. Which recombinant products can form?

items.title: Less help: test crossover position
items.prompt: Genes C and D are linked. A crossover occurs outside the interval containing both loci. What happens to the C-D combination on that chromatid?
options: It remains parental at C and D

items.title: Solo practice: distinguish structures
items.prompt: Which statement best describes the synaptonemal complex at this lesson’s scope?

items.title: Near exit: trace a single crossover
items.prompt: Linked alleles are M—N on one homolog and m—n on the other. A single crossover occurs between the loci. Which set includes recombinant chromatids?

items.title: Changed exit: trace two crossover points
items.prompt: Allele order is A—B—C. Two crossovers occur, one between A/B and one between B/C, on the same two non-sister chromatids. Which locus lies in the exchanged middle segment?

items.title: Repair: mark the interval
items.prompt: For linked loci P and Q, which crossover location can recombine their allele combination?
options: A crossover between P and Q
A cut on an unrelated chromosome

items.title: Fresh re-entry: new linked loci
items.prompt: One homolog carries R—S and the other r—s. A crossover lies between R and S. Which new combinations can appear?

items.title: Repair: bracket the double crossover
items.prompt: With order L—M—N, crossovers occur on both sides of M. Which segment should be traced as exchanged?

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry
items.prompt: A new map has order X—Y—Z with crossover points flanking Y. Which locus is inside the bounded exchange interval?

items.title: Starting check: follow a Y chromosome
items.prompt: An allele lies on a father’s Y chromosome. Which offspring can receive that chromosome from him?

items.title: Guided practice: follow a paternal X
items.prompt: A father carries an allele on his only X chromosome. Which offspring receive that X from him?

items.title: Less help: use chromosome location
items.prompt: Which observation is required before classifying a trait as X-linked in this lesson?
options: The allele lies on chromosome X

items.title: Solo practice: use Y constraints
items.prompt: Which transmission pattern is compatible with an allele located only on the Y chromosome?

items.title: Near exit: route an X-linked allele
items.prompt: A mother is heterozygous for an X-linked allele. Which statement is supported without assuming dominance?
options: Only daughters can receive her X
Only sons receive a maternal chromosome

items.title: Changed exit: switch to extranuclear inheritance
items.prompt: A heritable variant lies in an organelle genome contributed through the egg cytoplasm. Which parent-of-origin prediction fits?
options: Every father passes it to sons

items.title: Repair: separate paternal X and Y
items.prompt: In the modeled XY system, what does a father contribute to a daughter?

items.title: Fresh re-entry: new sex-linked route
items.prompt: A new allele is placed on a father’s X chromosome. Which offspring category necessarily receives that chromosome?

items.title: Repair: follow cytoplasm
items.prompt: Which information is decisive for a modeled extranuclear organelle variant?
options: Which parent contributes the Y only
Whether the nuclear allele is dominant

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry
items.prompt: A new variant is explicitly located in maternally contributed organelle DNA. Which route should be used?

items.title: Starting check: classify a replacement
items.prompt: A DNA segment changes from AACG to AATG at one position, with no length change. Which type is shown?

items.title: Guided practice: separate expression error
items.prompt: One ribosome inserts the wrong amino acid, but cellular DNA remains unchanged. Which description is most precise?

items.title: Less help: identify an insertion
items.prompt: An original sequence is ACTG and the altered sequence is ACATG. Which change occurred?

items.title: Solo practice: classify a reversed segment
items.prompt: A chromosome segment ordered A-B-C-D becomes A-C-B-D. Which structural change best fits?

items.title: Near exit: classify a moved segment
items.prompt: A segment leaves chromosome 2 and becomes attached to chromosome 5. Which type is shown?

items.title: Changed exit: use phenotype context
items.prompt: The same DNA substitution reduces activity of an enzyme that directly converts a precursor into a product. In the described environment, excess of that product is harmful. Which consequence is supported?

items.title: Repair: align the sequences
items.prompt: Original DNA is GCTA; altered DNA is GTA. Which change is present?

items.title: Fresh re-entry: classify a new sequence
items.prompt: Original DNA is TTAC; altered DNA is TTTAC. Which change occurred?

items.title: Repair: distinguish mutagen and carcinogen
items.prompt: Which statement correctly relates the terms without treating them as synonyms?

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry
items.prompt: A DNA deletion disrupts an enzyme in a required metabolic pathway. Which consequence is most directly supported?
options: The change is only a translation error
Cancer is the only possible outcome
